# DSH for VS Code 🐳
**English** | 中文
**DeepSeek Harness (DSH) inside VS Code.** Click the whale and get the full DSH web UI beside your c
ode — the extension starts or reuses `dsh web`, handles DSH's one-time-token authentication, and add
s native file, clipboard and image integration.
> ⭐ **If DSH saves you context switches, star the repo.** It is the simplest way to help more VS Cod
es you context switches, star the repo.** It is the simplest way to help more VS Code users find it.
Works with **DSH 0.1.2 and newer**, including its browser authentication (auto sign-in, no manual st
ep). Older DSH (≤ 0.1.1, no auth) keeps working. Both npm-installed `dsh` and DSH Desktop on Windows
(≤ 0.1.1, no auth) keeps working. Both npm-installed `dsh` and DSH Desktop on Windows are supported.
## 🚀 Quick start
1. **Install the extension** from the Marketplace, or run:

2. **Click the DSH whale** in the left Activity Bar or the right Secondary Side Bar.
3. **Done.** Th
e extension starts (or reuses) `dsh web`, signs the panel in, and shows DSH next to your code. No te
rminal, no browser tab, no manual login for a service it started itself.
**Prerequisite:** install the `dsh` CLI from DeepSeek Harness and put it on your PATH — or install D
SH Desktop on Windows. If `dsh` is missing, the extension shows a hint; `DSH: Show Logs` prints the
detected path, source and version.
Other ways to install (VSIX / from source)
**VSIX package:** download the latest `dsh-vscode.vsix` from Releases, then in VS Code run `Extensio
ns: Install from VSIX...` and reload the window.

## 🎯 Why DSH in VS Code?
| **Stay in the editor** | DSH lives in the sidebar or a side panel. Review code, run commands and t

alk to the agent without switching to a terminal or browser. |
| **Zero-config lifecycle** | The ext
ension detects the port, reuses an existing `dsh web`, or starts one silently and loads it once read

y. Closing the window stops only the service it started. |
| **Native editor integration** | A small
bridge makes file paths clickable in VS Code, opens external links in your browser, routes copy but

tons through the extension host, and restores undo/redo in the embedded page. |
| **Auth that just w
orks** | DSH ≥ 0.1.2 prints a one-time launch URL; the extension exchanges it for a 30-day session a

nd serves the panel through a local loopback relay, so the cross-site iframe keeps working. |
| **Wo
rks where you work** | Local, WSL, SSH Remote, Dev Containers and Codespaces (remote scenarios are o

pt-in via `dsh.remote.enabled`). |
| **Private by design** | Loopback addresses only (`127.0.0.1` /
`localhost` / `[::1]`); no credentials are read; the relay is not exposed to the network. |

## 🆕 What's new in 0.4.4
- **Accurate stopping state** (#40): when you click **Stop Service**, the panel now says “Stopping D

SH service…” and the status bar turns orange — it no longer pretends to be “Starting”.
- **DSH Deskt
op on a non-default drive** (#41): if Desktop is installed outside `%LOCALAPPDATA%` (for example `H:
\DeepSeek Harness`), the extension now uses the Desktop command already on PATH as a fallback instea

d of failing with `ENOENT`.
- This is a maintenance release; no new panels or commands. Full history

with `ENOENT`.
- This is a maintenance release; no new panels or commands. Full history: CHANGELOG.
## ✨ Features at a glance
| Feature | What you get |
| 🖱️ **One-click open** | A whale icon in the left Activity Bar and the right Secondary Side Bar; th

e editor title bar has a white-bg whale that opens the right-side panel. |
| 🚀 **Service management*
* | Auto-detect the port; reuse a running `dsh web`, otherwise start one in the background. Port con

flicts temporarily fall back to the first free port, with a notification. |
| 🛟 **Recoverable errors
** | Dedicated pages for missing `dsh`, occupied port, start timeout, crash and disconnect — each wi

th a one-click reconnect. |
| 🔐 **Auth relay** | Parses the one-time launch URL, stores a 30-day ses
sion cookie, and forwards the panel through a loopback relay. Externally started services get a one-

time paste page. |
| 🔗 **Bridge integration** | File paths open in VS Code, external links open in y

our browser, copy buttons work, and undo/redo is restored in the embedded page. |
| 🖼️ **Images with
out vision** | Attach images even when the active model has no vision: the image is cached in the wo
rkspace and sent as a file-path reference; the model reads it with an image tool. Opt out with `dsh.

image.fallback`. |
| 🌐 **Remote-ready** | SSH Remote, Dev Containers and Codespaces run `dsh` on the

remote and tunnel the panel; WSL works without a tunnel. |
| ⚙️ **Customizable** | Custom DSH profi
le, port, launch preference (npm / Desktop / auto), executable path, extra args, proxy env, timeout

and panel zoom. |
| 🌍 **Bilingual** | UI copy follows the VS Code display language: Chinese for `zh-
*`, English otherwise. |
## 🕹 Everyday use
[该节后续省略]
## 🏗 How it works
The extension owns the service lifecycle and a local relay. The panel is an iframe inside a VS Code
webview; the extension host talks to `dsh web` on `127.0.0.1`. The bridge runs inside the DSH page a
nd relays editor actions through `postMessage`.
## 🧭 Known limitations
- **Shift+drag from the VS Code Explorer (upstream)**: since VS Code 1.140, resource drags from the
Explorer no longer deliver `dragenter`/`dragover`/`drop` to a webview (microsoft/vscode#339278; the
upstream fix is still open). Use your system file manager or type `@` in the composer. Tracked in is

sue #37.
- **Image fallback needs a workspace folder**: files are cached under the workspace root; w
ith no folder open, the fallback is unavailable. Temporary images are cleaned up after use; `DSH: Cl

ean Up Image Cache` purges leftovers.
- **Externally started DSH (≥ 0.1.2)**: the extension cannot r
ead another process's log, so the first sign-in needs one paste of the launch URL (then up to 30 day
s). A service restart does not require pasting again.
